jobs.description:
AI Growth Marketer to own Livaclean's Shopify DTC channel — build landing pages with Claude CLI, create static ad variations at scale, and run A/B tests across the funnel. Livaclean is a 7-year-old ecommerce skincare brand (pimple patches, face care, hair care) with a fully remote team across Pakistan, Philippines, India, and LATAM.

The Role

We're a 95% Amazon business building our DTC/Shopify channel (~$25K/month today). This is an experimental, builder-stage role you're not maintaining a system, you're creating one. Claude CLI proficiency is a hard requirement.

You'll own the static ad pipeline: produce 20-50 AI-powered ad variations/week, test messaging across awareness levels, and feed winning data to our video creative team. 500+ UGC videos/month already flowing in for creative mining.

What You'll Do

Build and optimize Shopify landing pages, PDPs, and advertorials using Claude CLI (~30%)

Create 20-50 static ad variations/week using AI tools — test hooks across problem/solution/product-aware audiences (~30%)

Run A/B tests across pages, ads, and email — track CTR, CPA, ROAS, and conversion rates (~20%)

Optimize Klaviyo email flows (welcome, abandoned cart, post-purchase) (~10%)

Develop ad concepts at volume, mine UGC library, collaborate with Creative Lead (~10%)

Requirements

Must-Have:

Claude CLI proficiency (this is non-negotiable)

Marketing fundamentals: awareness levels, funnels, A/B testing, ad performance analysis

Shopify experience (PDP editing, DTC ecommerce flows)

AI-powered static ad creation at volume (portfolio required)

Data-driven, self-directed, comfortable building from scratch

Nice-to-Have:

Klaviyo or email marketing experience

Meta Ads, Google Ads, or TikTok Ads manager

DTC CRO, A/B testing tools (VWO, Optimizely)

HTML/CSS, skincare/beauty category experience

Working Arrangement

1-month paid trial full-time, with growth into DTC Growth Lead

Fully remote, a sync-first, 4 hours/week CT overlap for syncs

We cover all AI tools, Shopify apps, and software — you choose the stack

Direct founder access, full autonomy over workflow

To Apply:

1. Claude CLI demo (mandatory) — Loom video showing you building something with Claude CLI

2. Marketing portfolio — landing pages, static ads, email campaigns, Shopify work. Specialist in one area? Show depth, not breadth

3. Pick any Livaclean product — mock up 1 static ad concept for 3 awareness levels (problem/solution/product-aware)

jobs.description:
Job Title

Director, Transaction Management

Job Description Summary

As the Transaction Management Director, you will lead transaction management strategy and execution for large, complex client portfolios and enterprise real estate initiatives across multiple asset classes. This role translates client business objectives into market optimization strategies, transaction plans, portfolio opportunities, and high-quality execution outcomes while leading brokerage resources, transaction teams, and cross-functional partners.

As a member of Cushman & Wakefield’s Portfolio Advisory Group, the Transaction Management Director will be dedicated to one or more of Cushman & Wakefield’s most dynamic client accounts. In this role, you will collaborate closely with peers and the account team to support a client's strategic real estate vision. The Transaction Management Director will embody our team philosophy “Client First, Insight Always, Execution Excellence”, ensuring every deliverable reflects the team’s commitment to innovation, collaboration, and measurable impact.

Job Description

Strategic Portfolio & Market Optimization

  • Lead market optimization planning and strategic transaction initiatives that align with client business goals, portfolio objectives, and real estate priorities.

  • Lead development of strategic real estate plans and provide strategic real estate advice to clients.

  • Identify occupancy cost savings strategies, pull-forward opportunities, expansion and contraction strategies, and other portfolio optimization opportunities.

  • Produce and support business case development, reporting, data analysis, and financial analysis required to complete strategic plans.

Complex Transaction Leadership & Execution

  • Initiate new transactions, dispositions, and renewals, and guide transaction delivery through execution.

  • Manage internal and third-party brokerage resources through the course of transactions, providing strategic direction to brokers and client stakeholders.

  • Lead and oversee aggressive negotiations to deliver favorable outcomes on behalf of the client and support consistent transaction management practices.

  • Execute complex, large transactions with high-level transaction knowledge and oversee legal review of client leased documents.

  • Engage project managers, facility managers, environmental consultants, and other partners as needed to support transaction execution.

Client Relationship & Transaction Governance

  • Partner with client corporate real estate teams and local business unit leaders to understand requirements and build transaction strategies that support client needs.

  • Lead and facilitate client presentations, business reviews, key client meetings, and transaction governance discussions.

  • Partner with clients’ senior-level operational groups to identify real estate needs, transaction priorities, and areas of opportunity.

Reporting, Financial Analysis & Value Creation

  • Maintain and monitor process reporting to clients using a variety of tools and ensure accurate transaction data using various systems.

  • Perform market and financial analysis to support transaction strategy, portfolio recommendations, and client decision making.

  • Manage revenue projections and tracking to support account-level visibility and performance management

  • .

  • Prepare close-out reports and value-add calculations for transactions.

Process Governance, Technology & AI Enablement

  • Coordinate reporting requirements and provide guidance to field agents, service partners, and clients to maximize reporting effectiveness.

  • Modify and adapt process documents and playbooks to meet client requirements.

  • Identify and implement process improvements, innovations, post-transaction reviews, and client survey practices that support continuous improvement.

  • Leverage AI-enabled and technology-driven solutions to improve transaction execution, reporting quality, analysis, workflow efficiency, and client outcomes.

People Leadership & Team Development

  • Manage direct reports through coaching and mentoring to support an engaged, high-performing transaction management team.

  • Lead transaction teams, brokers, field agents, service partners, and cross-functional contributors through complex transaction activity.

  • Maintain a cohesive, performance-measured team environment that supports client satisfaction, work quality, and consistent delivery.




Cushman & Wakefield also provides eligible employees with an opportunity to enroll in a variety of benefit programs, generally including health, vision, and dental insurance, flexible spending accounts, health savings accounts, retirement savings plans, life, and disability insurance programs, and paid and unpaid time away from work. In addition to a comprehensive benefits package, Cushman and Wakefield provide eligible employees with competitive pay, which may vary depending on eligibility factors such as geographic location, date of hire, total hours worked, job type, business line, and applicability of collective bargaining agreements.
The compensation that will be offered to the successful candidate will depend on factors such as whether the position is covered by a collective bargaining agreement, the geographic area in which the work will be performed, market pay rates in that area, and the candidate’s experience and qualifications.
The company will not pay less than minimum wage for this role.

Overview

DecisionPoint seeks a Data Analyst (Reporting) to develop KPI frameworks, analyze operational and performance data, and produce recurring reports for a large federal and DoD-aligned mission environment. This role is responsible for generating weekly and monthly performance reports, tracking service-level agreements (SLAs), analyzing alert trends, and identifying areas for system and operational improvement.

The Data Analyst supports the PMO, dashboard teams, engineering teams, and operations staff by transforming raw operational data into clear, actionable insights. This includes KPI development, trend identification, and metric reconciliation to ensure reporting accuracy across the enterprise.

This position is fully remote.

Duties & Responsibilities

The Data Analyst (Reporting) will:

  • Develop KPI calculations and performance measurement frameworks.
  • Track SLA performance and identify deviations, risks, or improvement opportunities.
  • Analyze monitoring alerts, incidents, performance logs, and operational data for trends.
  • Prepare weekly, monthly, and quarterly analytic reports and executive summaries.
  • Support dashboard teams in defining metrics, data sources, and visualization requirements.
  • Conduct data validation, reconciliation, and quality checks across multiple data sources.
  • Perform ad hoc analyses to support operations, engineering, and leadership decision-making.
  • Maintain reporting templates, standards, and metadata definitions.
  • Identify anomalies, performance bottlenecks, and recurring issues.
  • Document analytic processes and ensure alignment with program reporting requirements.

Qualifications

Clearance Requirement

Candidate must possess an active Secret clearance or higher.

Education (Required)

Bachelor’s degree in Data Analytics, Mathematics, Data Science, or a closely related field.

Experience (Required)

  • Minimum 5 years of experience performing reporting, analytics, or data analysis.
  • Experience developing KPIs and tracking SLA performance.
  • Experience producing weekly/monthly reports for federal, DoD, or large enterprise environments.
  • Experience analyzing alert logs, incidents, or operational performance datasets.

Technical Knowledge (Required)

  • Proficiency with Excel, SQL, or analytical tools for data querying and reporting.
  • Understanding of KPI design, SLA metrics, and performance measurement methodologies.
  • Familiarity with dashboards or BI tools like Power BI, Tableau, or Grafana.
  • Knowledge of data validation, reconciliation, and quality control principles.

Technical Knowledge (Preferred)

  • Experience with cloud-based analytics or log aggregation tools.
  • Familiarity with scripting for automation (Python, R, etc.).

Certifications

Required:

  • ITIL Foundation

Preferred:

  • Data analytics or BI tool certifications

Skills

  • Strong analytical and quantitative reasoning abilities.
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills for executive reporting.
  • High attention to detail and accuracy in reporting outputs.
  • Ability to identify trends, anomalies, and insights across complex datasets.
  • Strong time management and ability to handle recurring deadlines.

NRG is seeking a Director to join its Growth & Partnerships organization. This role is ideal for an analytically rigorous energy leader who excels at creating structure, aligning cross-functional teams, and establishing repeatable processes that improve how complex opportunities are evaluated and advanced.

The Director will build the internal programs, decision systems, governance, and analytical standards that enable the Growth & Partnerships organization to execute consistently and at a high level. This leader will create the structure, cross-functional alignment, and operating discipline needed to translate complex growth opportunities into clear priorities, rigorous analysis, and executable plans.

Working across internal functions, the Director will create consistency across opportunity portfolios, and ensure leaders receive comparable, decision-ready analysis. The role will partner closely with NRG’s operating businesses and Finance, Regulatory, Legal, Operations, Technology, Development, and other functions to move priority opportunities through a clear, disciplined path from initial thesis to validation, investment decision, and transition to scale.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design and manage a common operating system for the Growth & Partnerships organization, including opportunity intake, prioritization, workplans, stage gates, decision rights, governance forums, and transition criteria.

  • Create and drive decision-making systems that help leadership allocate resources, resolve tradeoffs, and advance the highest-value opportunities with discipline.

  • Establish a consistent analytical framework for evaluating opportunities across markets, business units, technologies, and time horizons.

  • Set and uphold a high bar for business cases, financial models, market assessments, customer value propositions, risk analysis, and executive recommendations; ensure assumptions and logic are transparent and defensible.

  • Integrate opportunity portfolios into a coherent enterprise pipeline, enabling teams to focus on developing opportunities while maintaining consistent priorities, processes, and execution standards across the organization.

  • Lead cross-functional growth programs that bring together commercial, Finance, Regulatory, Legal, Operations, Technology, Development, Strategy, and business-unit teams around shared outcomes.

  • Build trusted internal relationships, clarify roles and accountabilities, surface dependencies, and create practical pathways through organizational complexity.

  • Develop reusable tools, templates, data standards, and reporting mechanisms that improve the quality, consistency, and speed of work across the organization.

  • Maintain enterprise visibility into portfolio status, resource needs, risks, open questions, milestones, and upcoming decisions.

  • Translate complex cross-functional work into clear, executive-ready materials and integrated recommendations for senior leadership and Board discussions.

  • Support pilot governance and transition planning so validated opportunities move cleanly to the business units best positioned to scale them.

What We Are Looking For

  • Enterprise operators who know how to build the programs, processes, and operating rhythms that make a new organization effective.

  • Patient bridge-builders who can establish trust, navigate internally, and align stakeholders with different goals, constraints, and perspectives.

  • Structured problem solvers who turn ambiguity into practical workplans, decision frameworks, governance, and clear accountability.

  • Analytically rigorous leaders who remain close enough to the work to test the logic, challenge assumptions, and raise the quality of models and recommendations.

  • Cross-functional leaders who create momentum through influence, follow-through, and disciplined coordination rather than formal authority.

  • Systems thinkers who can identify common requirements across distinct opportunity portfolios while preserving appropriate flexibility.

  • Strong communicators who translate complex technical, regulatory, operational, and financial issues into clear choices for senior stakeholders.

  • Collaborative peers who complement externally oriented growth leaders and take pride in enabling the entire team to perform at a consistently high level.

  • Leaders who demonstrate sound judgment, intellectual honesty, ownership, persistence, and a commitment to measurable outcomes.

Preferred Experience

  • 10–15+ years of experience in enterprise strategy, program leadership, strategic finance, management consulting, operations, business transformation, market development, or a related field.

  • Demonstrated experience creating and implementing decision systems, governance models, stage gates, portfolio processes, or other operating mechanisms for complex cross-functional work.

  • Recent hands-on experience building or reviewing sophisticated financial models and analytical frameworks, with the ability to understand the underlying logic rather than simply replicate an existing analysis.

  • Significant experience in energy, utilities, competitive power markets, distributed energy resources, demand response, energy technology, infrastructure, data centers, industrial energy management, or a closely related sector.

  • Technical knowledge of energy markets, including regulated ecosystems, and the ability to quickly understand complex commercial, regulatory, operational, and financial environments.

  • Experience leading cross-functional initiatives and influencing senior stakeholders without relying on direct authority.

  • Experience standardizing methods, data, assumptions, reporting, or decision criteria across teams or business units.

  • Familiarity with one or more of the following areas: wholesale power and generation economics; retail energy and customer solutions; data center and hyperscaler energy needs; utility partnerships and regulation; DERs, demand response, load flexibility, or virtual power plants; corporate development, investment analysis, or commercialization of new products and services.

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Economics, Engineering, Energy Systems, Public Policy, or a related discipline.

  • MBA, master’s degree, or other advanced degree preferred but not required.

Success in This Role

  • Establish a trusted, repeatable operating system that gives Growth & Partnerships a shared language, cadence, and path from opportunity intake through decision and transition.

  • Create consistent analytical and decision standards across opportunity portfolios and supporting teams.

  • Enable teams to develop clear, comparable business cases, financial models, assumptions, and executive recommendations that support effective enterprise decision-making.

jobs.description:
Engineering Lead

Large, Complex Federal Government Program | Full-Time W-2 | Fully Remote (U.S.)

The Problem We're Hiring You to Solve

Monthly production releases. Zero escaped critical defects. Most engineering organizations treat those as a tradeoff. On this program they are both commitments, measured every release, in front of the customer.

We are hiring the engineering leader who builds an organization that delivers both at once: multiple cross-functional development teams modernizing a federal home loan benefit platform while sustaining the 20-year-old system it replaces. If you believe speed and quality are the same discipline practiced well, and you have the delivery record to prove it, keep reading.

The Opportunity

Most engineering leadership roles ask you to protect a delivery machine someone else built. This one asks you to build the machine.

The program spans multiple development teams working in parallel across a modern platform (Salesforce-centered, configuration-first, supplemented by serverless capabilities in a government cloud) and a legacy suite that must stay stable until it is decommissioned. Work arrives through a formal intake process that turns business needs into executable plans with committed scope, timelines, and team sizing in days. Then your organization delivers against those commitments, publicly and measurably.

The quality bar is unusually explicit. Every release ships with 100% automated test coverage for its features before user acceptance testing begins. Defect detection before UAT must exceed 95%. Escaped critical defects must be zero. Critical production bugs get fixed in three days. Accessibility and security compliance are release gates, not aspirations. These are not stretch goals on a slide. They are how the program measures the engineering organization every month.

That bar is exactly why this role is interesting. Hitting it once takes heroics. Hitting it every month takes an engineering system: disciplined definition of done, test automation as a first-class craft, engineers who own quality instead of throwing code over a wall, and a leader who builds all of that into how teams work rather than inspecting it in afterward. That leader is you.

You will work alongside a Senior DevSecOps & Platform Engineering Lead who owns the delivery pipeline and an Enterprise Solution Architect who owns the designs. You own the organization that turns those designs into shipped, tested, production software.

What You'll Own

  • The engineering organization. Lead multiple cross-functional development teams across modern and legacy platforms, flexing team size and composition as workflows through intake. Teams form, deliver, and re-form around the work. You make that fluid instead of chaotic.
  • Delivery you put your name on. Commit to scope, level of effort, and timelines in executable plans, then hit them. When you cannot, say so early, with a recovery plan, before the customer discovers it.
  • A quality system, not a QA gate. Engineer quality into how teams work: definition of done that includes full automated testing, code review that catches problems, and metrics that surface risk early. The outcomes that prove it: zero escaped critical defects, defect detection above 95% before UAT, and critical fixes inside three days.
  • Test automation as a craft. Build the discipline where every feature ships with complete positive and negative automated coverage, and the regression suite becomes the safety net the customer trusts enough to focus UAT on new functionality only.
  • The monthly release drumbeat. Production value ships every 30 days or faster, release after release, without burning the team down to do it.
  • Dual-stack engineering. Run modern configuration-first platform development and legacy sustainment side by side, including the warranty on everything your teams release.
  • Engineering standards that outlast you. Set and enforce the bar for code quality, review, documentation, and definition of done across every team, and keep documentation current with every release because the program requires it and good engineering does too.
  • AI-native development at team scale. Make AI-assisted engineering the norm across your organization, not the hobby of your three most curious engineers, while holding AI-assisted work to the same zero-escaped-defect bar as everything else.
  • The talent engine. Hire deliberately, grow engineers visibly, retain the strong ones, and raise the bar with every addition.

AI-Native Engineering at Team Scale

AI is part of how PhoenixTeam works. Plenty of leaders can use AI tools themselves. This role is about something harder: making an entire engineering organization genuinely better with them.

We are looking for someone who already uses tools like Claude Code, Cursor, or GitHub Copilot in their own work, and who has begun leading teams through the shift: establishing standards for responsible AI-assisted development, using AI to expand automated test coverage and accelerate code review, applying it to defect analysis and documentation, and measuring whether it actually improved throughput and quality rather than assuming it did.

The accountability question matters most in a federal environment with a zero-escaped-critical-defect standard. AI-generated code is your teams' code. It gets the same review, the same testing, and the same ownership as anything an engineer typed by hand. You set that culture.

Boundaries are non-negotiable: federal environments govern what tools may touch government code, systems, and data. Use AI wherever it creates leverage, and understand the security, data, privacy, and authorization boundaries governing where and how it can be used.

Tools will change. The leadership behavior we are hiring for will not: continually ask where your organization's engineering hours are going and eliminate the waste responsibly.

What Great Looks Like

Twelve months in, we would expect to see:

  1. The cadence held. Production value shipped at least monthly, every month, with zero escaped critical defects and a team that is energized rather than exhausted.
  2. The regression suite earned trust. Automated coverage is complete enough that UAT focuses on new features, and the customer stopped asking whether old functionality still works.
  3. Quality metrics are boring in the best way. Detection rates above 95%, critical fixes inside three days, and defect trends the customer reviews without concern.
  4. Teams flex without drama. Work moves from intake to a staffed, productive team quickly, and re-forming teams around new work stopped being disruptive.
  5. AI lifted the organization measurably. Throughput and coverage improved with AI-assisted engineering, defect rates did not, and your standards for responsible use became the program's standards.
  6. Both stacks are healthy. Legacy sustainment is quiet and predictable while modern platform velocity grows quarter over quarter.
  7. The bench is stronger. Engineers you hired and grew are visibly better, your leads lead, and departures are rare and regretted.
  8. The customer asks for more. Delivery confidence earned the program expanded scope.

What You Bring

We care about evidence more than resumes. Expect us to ask what your organizations shipped, what your defect and delivery metrics actually were, how you turned around a team that was missing its commitments, and how AI functions across your teams today.

  • A multi-team delivery record. You have led engineering organizations of multiple teams building and shipping production software, and you can walk us through the delivery and quality outcomes with numbers.
  • Hands-on credibility. You still read code, review designs, and go deep when it matters. Engineers respect your technical judgment, not just your title.
  • A quality system you built. You have taken an organization to measurably low defect escape rates through engineering discipline and test automation, not through more manual QA at the end.
  • Federal delivery experience. You have shipped software inside a regulated federal environment and treat security, accessibility, authorization, and documentation requirements as delivery constraints to engineer within, not excuses for slipping.
  • Metrics fluency. You run engineering organizations on evidence: release cadence, defect detection and escape rates, cycle times, automation coverage, and you use those numbers to improve the system rather than to punish people.
  • AI-forward leadership. You use AI engineering tools yourself and have led teams into using them well, with standards, measurement, and accountability.
  • Customer-facing composure. You present delivery status, defend engineering decisions with evidence, deliver bad news early, and challenge unrealistic direction respectfully, including ours.
  • Talent judgment. You hire well, grow engineers deliberately, and make hard calls about performance without outsourcing them to HR processes.

  • U.S.-based, and able to obtain and maintain a federal Public Trust clearance.

We do not screen on degrees or year counts. If your evidence is strong, we want to talk.

Helpful, Not Required

  • Salesforce delivery leadership, or leadership of teams on a comparable configuration-first enterprise platform.
  • Deep background in test automation frameworks and strategy.
  • Experience running legacy sustainment and modernization in parallel, or decommissioning a production system.
  • Familiarity with 508 accessibility compliance in delivery.
  • Mortgage or housing finance experience is not required. We will teach you the domain.

Leadership Expectations

This is an organizational leadership role with a hands-on soul.

You own outcomes across multiple teams, which means your leverage comes through leads, standards, and systems rather than personal output. But you stay close enough to the work to know when a design is wrong, an estimate is padded, or a team is quietly drowning. Engineers should experience you as a leader who understands what they do, because you can still do it.

You work directly with federal customers and decision-makers. You present delivery status with candor, defend your teams' engineering decisions with evidence, and challenge poor technical or program direction respectfully. Silent disagreement is a failure mode here, and so is shielding the customer from bad news until it becomes a crisis.

You develop the leaders under you deliberately, and you hold the engineering bar even when the schedule argues against it, because on this program the quality metrics are the schedule.

You'll Probably Love This Role If...

You are the leader whose teams ship on a rhythm others find implausible, and you can explain exactly which disciplines make it possible. You think a public, measured quality bar is a gift, because it settles arguments that consume other organizations. You would rather build a delivery machine than inherit one. You like customers in the room. And you are genuinely energized by leading engineers through the AI shift, because you have seen what it does for a team that adopts it seriously.

This May Not Be the Role for You If...

We would rather you self-select now than be unhappy in month three. You may struggle here if you:

  • Lead from dashboards and status meetings, and stopped engaging with the actual engineering.
  • Treat quality as the QA team's job rather than an engineering outcome you own.
  • Negotiate quality bars down when schedules get tight.
  • Hide delivery risk from customers until it becomes undeniable.
  • Prefer stable, fixed teams and find flexing around the work disruptive.
  • View AI as a novelty rather than an engineering capability your organization must master.
  • Stopped learning when you became senior.

None of that makes someone a bad leader. It makes them a bad fit for this particular job.

Why PhoenixTeam

  • We are practitioners, not a staffing shop. PhoenixTeam is a woman-owned small business founded and led by housing finance technologists who still do the work. Our teams have spent years embedded inside federal housing programs, from loan guaranty to rural housing lending to mortgage insurance. You will build your organization alongside leaders who have shipped, not above account managers who have not.
  • Your leadership has visible consequences. Delivery cadence, quality, and reliability are measured monthly and reviewed by the customer. The organization you build performs in public.
  • Direct customer access. You work with federal decision-makers yourself. Your judgment reaches the people who act on it, without three layers of translation in between.
  • You build the machine. You are establishing how engineering delivery works on this program, not maintaining someone else's operating model.
  • AI-native is practice, not positioning. AI is part of how PhoenixTeam delivers, and we fund ongoing AI education and development for the entire team. In this role you will scale that investment across an organization, not fight for permission to use it.
  • Fully remote,S.-based, permanently.
  • Competitive salary and 100% employer-paid medical insurance.
  • Mission you can explain at dinner. The software your teams ship supports a home loan benefit for the people who served this country.

Position Requirements

  • Full-time W-2 employment with PhoenixTeam.
  • Must be based in the United States.
  • Fully remote.
  • Work supports a federal civilian agency.
  • Must be able to obtain and maintain the required federal Public Trust clearance. A Secret clearance is not required.

PhoenixTeam is a woman-owned small business focused on federal and commercial housing finance technology.

Responsibilities

Peraton's Department of the Interior (DOI), U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (FWS), and NOAA's National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS) have identified a critical gap in the federal government's ability to conduct comprehensive Endangered Species Act (ESA) research. While FWS operates an authoritative web-based platform for managing data for terrestrial and freshwater species, it does not currently include NMFS marine and anadromous species data forcing agencies to rely on separate, manual processes. This program closes that gap by integrating marine and anadromous species data into the existing FWS platform, creating a single, unified experience for all ESA-listed species.

Peraton is seeking a Senior Cloud Data Architect SME with expertise in Databricks and cloud data lakehouse architectures to lead the data engineering foundation for a federal data migration program.   • Lead schema harmonization activities, conducting gap analysis between source schemas and the target data model and producing field-level mapping documentation

  • Lead the operational handoff of ETL pipeline architecture, producing documentation for routine data refresh, pipeline monitoring, and maintenance procedures

jobs.description:
Fractional HR Officer (6–8 Hours per Week) – FinTech / Remote

PLEASE READ THE FULL JOB DESCRIPTION BEFORE APPLYING

Location: Remote
Working Pattern: Fractional – approximately 6–8 hours per week
Environment: Early-Stage FinTech / People Operations

About the Opportunity

Our client is an early-stage FinTech currently building out its team, leadership capability and internal infrastructure.

As part of this development, the company is looking for a Fractional HR Officer to provide practical People Operations support under the direction of an experienced senior People leader.

This opportunity is particularly suited to an early-career HR professional who already has some practical HR experience but is looking to broaden their exposure, develop their capability and take on increasing responsibility.

You will gain exposure to a wide range of People activity within an early-stage organisation, including recruitment, onboarding, People administration, documentation, employee/consultant records and the development of People processes.

This is not an opportunity for somebody seeking purely observational HR experience. You will be expected to contribute practically, take responsibility for agreed tasks and handle sensitive information appropriately.

In return, there is significant opportunity to learn, develop and gain exposure to the practical development of a People function from an early stage.

Further details regarding the engagement and participation structure will be discussed directly with candidates progressing through the process.

Application – Mandatory Qualifying Questions

Please submit your CV together with a cover letter. Within your cover letter, you must answer each of the mandatory qualifying questions below.

  1. What practical HR or People Operations experience do you currently have? Please describe your responsibilities rather than simply providing your job title.
  2. What CIPD qualification have you completed or are you currently studying? Please state whether this is CIPD Level 3 or Level 5, together with your expected completion date if you are still studying.
  3. What experience do you have supporting employee, worker or contractor onboarding and offboarding?
  4. What experience do you have maintaining confidential People records, HR documentation or personnel files?
  5. What recruitment administration or coordination experience do you have?
  6. Please provide an example of an HR/People process that you have personally administered from beginning to end.
  7. This role involves handling confidential employee, candidate and business information. Please describe your experience handling sensitive information and how you ensure confidentiality and accuracy.
  8. What are you hoping to learn or develop through an opportunity like this?
  9. This opportunity requires approximately 6–8 hours per week. Can you consistently commit to this level of involvement alongside your other professional or study commitments?

These questions are mandatory and form part of our initial assessment process. Applications that do not provide a clear answer to every mandatory qualifying question will be automatically disqualified and will not be considered further in the recruitment process.

What You'll Be Doing

Working under the direction of senior People leadership, you will provide practical support across the developing People function.

Your responsibilities are likely to include:

  • Supporting recruitment administration and coordination
  • Maintaining candidate and recruitment trackers
  • Coordinating interviews and recruitment documentation
  • Supporting onboarding and offboarding processes
  • Maintaining accurate People records
  • Organising employee and consultant documentation
  • Monitoring outstanding documentation and following up where required
  • Supporting contract and People-document administration
  • Maintaining appropriate People trackers and audit trails
  • Drafting routine People correspondence
  • Supporting the organisation and maintenance of People policies and processes
  • Helping maintain accurate records relating to confidentiality and other engagement documentation
  • Supporting document control and appropriate record keeping
  • Undertaking People research where required
  • Providing general People Operations support
  • Taking increasing ownership of agreed processes as your capability develops

What We're Looking For

This is a developmental opportunity, but some existing HR knowledge and practical experience is required.

You should have:

  • Previous practical HR / People Operations experience
  • A CIPD Level 3 or Level 5 qualification, completed or currently being studied
  • Understanding of core employment and HR processes
  • Strong administration and organisational skills
  • Excellent attention to detail
  • Confidence working with confidential information
  • Good written communication
  • Ability to follow processes and instructions accurately
  • Willingness to ask questions when something is unclear
  • Ability to manage agreed tasks independently
  • Genuine interest in developing a career within HR / People
  • Comfort working within an early-stage environment where processes are still being developed

Experience within technology, FinTech, financial services, startups or another regulated environment would be useful but is not essential.

We are more interested in finding someone with the right HR foundations, judgement, reliability and desire to develop.

Why This Opportunity?

Unlike an HR role within a large established organisation where responsibilities may be limited to one narrow area, this opportunity offers exposure to the development of a People function from an early stage.

You will have the opportunity to:

  • Work directly with experienced senior People leadership
  • Develop practical People Operations experience
  • Gain exposure across recruitment and the employee/consultant lifecycle
  • Learn how People infrastructure is created and scaled
  • Develop experience within an early-stage FinTech environment
  • Take on increasing responsibility as your capability develops

For the right person, this should provide considerably broader exposure than a narrowly defined junior HR position within a large organisation.

Engagement Structure

This is a flexible, fractional engagement of approximately 6–8 hours per week within an early-stage FinTech venture.

It is particularly suited to someone who wants to develop their HR career while participating in the development of a growing organisation alongside other compatible professional or study commitments.

The engagement is structured around participation in the longer-term development and growth of the business rather than a conventional employment package at this stage.

Full details of the participation structure will be discussed with candidates progressing through the process.

jobs.excerpt: Cheesecake Labs is an AI, data, and product engineering partner for established and scaling organizations navigating legacy systems, fragmented data, AI pressure, or limited engineering capacity.
jobs.description:
Cheesecake Labs is an AI, data, and product engineering partner for established and scaling organizations navigating legacy systems, fragmented data, AI pressure, or limited engineering capacity.

Our services include AI Implementation, Application Modernization, Data & Analytics, Product Engineering, AI-Accelerated Delivery, and Embedded Engineering Teams. We deliver agentic workflows in 8-12 weeks and modernize applications in 5-10 months rather than 2 years. We also build trusted data foundations and digital products designed to scale. Our agentic software development lifecycle accelerates execution, while experienced engineers embed with client teams to provide technical depth, security, and clear ownership.

Member of Anthropic's Claude Partner Network; technology partners include Databricks, Snowflake, dbt, and AWS.

Across 13+ years, Cheesecake Labs has built 300+ products for clients including Eurasia Group, MoneyGram, the World Bank, Stellar, Wedgewood, PepsiCo, Merck, Sodexo, and Mercado Libre.

The story behind this role

At Cheesecake Labs, our designers don’t just create screens.

We’re usually brought in when products are still evolving, requirements are not fully defined yet, and teams need to balance user experience, business priorities, technical constraints, and delivery speed all at the same time.

Many of our client engagements start with strategic conversations and evolve quickly into active projects.

That’s why we maintain a network of strong contractor designers we can engage quickly when the right projects come in.

This is not a traditional long-term internal role.

It’s a contractor opportunity designed for people who enjoy working across different products, clients, industries, and business challenges in fast-moving environments.

We’re looking for a Senior Product Designer (Contractor) who combines strong product thinking, visual design skills, user empathy, and ownership across the full product design lifecycle.

Engagement details

  • Contractor / project-based engagement
  • Paid in USD/hour
  • Remote-first
  • Flexible allocation depending on project availability and fit
  • Opportunities may vary in duration, scope, and weekly commitment depending on client needs

Some opportunities may start immediately.
Others may become active as new projects enter our pipeline.

What this role actually looks like

This is not a “just receive requirements and design screens” type of role.

On a typical project, you might:

  • Work closely with team members to shape product experiences and figure out what should actually be built
  • Conduct user research, market research, and validation activities when needed
  • Break down product requirements and user stories into practical design flows and experiences
  • Create high-quality UI designs, mockups, prototypes, and scalable design systems
  • Balance usability, business priorities, technical constraints, and delivery timelines in day-to-day decisions
  • Participate in product and design discussions with international clients and multidisciplinary teams

Some projects will be highly execution-focused.
Others will involve broader discovery, product strategy, and UX decision-making.

Most are a mix of both.

What tends to work well here

We’ve seen that people who thrive in this type of engagement usually:

  • Have strong experience designing digital products across web and mobile environments
  • Feel comfortable navigating both UX and UI challenges — from discovery and flows to polished interfaces and interactions
  • Have a collaborative mindset and work well alongside engineers, product managers, and stakeholders
  • Feel comfortable navigating ambiguity, evolving requirements, and fast-changing product contexts
  • Care deeply about usability, design quality, consistency, and pragmatic product decisions
  • Feel totally confident working in English with international clients and teams (calls, discussions, async) — at least advanced level
  • Already use AI as part of their day-to-day workflow — whether for research, ideation, prototyping, content support, or workflow acceleration

Experience with modern design systems, mobile design guidelines, or tools such as Figma, Sketch, Zeplin, Adobe products, or similar platforms is a strong plus.

This probably won’t be your thing if

Just to be transparent:

  • You’re looking for a highly stable long-term internal role with fixed scope and predictable allocation
  • You prefer highly structured environments with rigid processes and very defined requirements
  • You’re uncomfortable navigating ambiguity or fast-changing product contexts
  • You’d rather avoid collaboration with engineers, product teams, or clients
  • You dislike balancing business constraints, user needs, and delivery realities simultaneously

There’s nothing wrong with any of that — it’s just not how these engagements usually operate.

One last thing

To participate in this selection process, you must:

  • Have a valid business registration in your country (CNPJ, VAT, EIN, or equivalent)
  • Have a bank account eligible to receive USD payments
  • Be able to issue invoices accordingly

These requirements are necessary for contractor engagement and payment processing.

Not sure if you check every box?

That’s okay.

We know that many great people — especially from underrepresented groups — hesitate to apply unless they meet 100% of the requirements.

If this opportunity sounds interesting, we’d still love to hear from you.

IMPORTANT TIP -> The communication during the selection process is done by email. We suggest that you keep an eye on your email inboxes and set the permission to receive messages from @cheesecakelabs.hire.trakstar.com so our messages will not be directed to the spam box ;)

The collected personal data will be used only to manage and control candidate resumes in order to assess the necessary requirements such as the contact information, and also to conduct this selection process.

The collected data will not be shared with others (“third parties”) without your authorization, and their use will be restricted to Cheesecake Labs internal staff, and also to the service providers that process your data for the selection process. At any time, you can contact us and we will remove your data from our data collection system. In order to do that, just simply send an email to .

jobs.description:
Vice President, Software Engineering — Seven Bridges

Location: Remote. US preferred. India or EMEA candidates considered.

Reports to: Chief Technology Officer

Who are we?

Velsera is the precision engine company. We build the software researchers, scientists, and clinicians use to drive precision R&D and bring analytics closer to the point of care. Seven Bridges, Pierian, and UgenTec came together to form Velsera; we are headquartered in Boston, MA, with [current headcount] colleagues across [current country count] countries.

The Seven Bridges Platform is our research genomics platform — roughly 130 containerized services, multi-cloud, running in commercial and FedRAMP Moderate environments, where scientists run CWL, WDL, and Nextflow workflows over petabyte-scale genomic data. Current priorities are federated data management, compliance as a product capability, and governed AI.

Reporting line and scope

You report to the CTO and own engineering for the Seven Bridges Platform: architecture, delivery, and production operations, including reliability, cost, technical debt, and observability. The team is primarily in India, with a smaller group in Serbia; you lead across both sites and work daily with stakeholders in other time zones. You hold architecture authority for the platform, co-own boundary decisions with security, federal compliance, and quality leadership, and partner with a cross-business AI Engineering team.

The role is roughly 40% hands-on technical work and 60% people leadership and organizational delivery. Hands-on means owning architecture decisions of record, leading design reviews, reviewing code and infrastructure changes, and prototyping where needed. You should be credible to your most senior engineers, with a clear view of what this class of platform should become and the ability to take a team and a business there.

What will you do?

  • Own the technical vision for the platform over the next three years, and turn it into an architecture and roadmap the team and the business believe in.
  • Own architecture decisions of record, design reviews, multi-tenant isolation, and complexity reduction across the service estate.
  • Keep delivery governed and modern: infrastructure-as-code under CI with policy-as-code, short-lived credentials, progressive rollout, and change evidence that holds up to audit in a federally authorized environment.
  • Own reliability: SLOs and error budgets on the paths customers depend on, on-call design that works across two sites, and turning repeat incidents into architectural change.
  • Ship governed AI in the product and apply AI to how the team builds, both under a governance policy co-owned with Risk & Compliance, and both measured.
  • Build the team: management depth you can trust with delivery, the specialist skills the roadmap needs, and maintaining a thriving team through a period of growth.

Requirements

What do you bring to the table?

Must have

  1. 12+ years in software engineering, including several years leading multi-team organizations through managers.
  1. Distributed-systems and platform architecture ownership at scale — multi-tenant isolation, service decomposition, and the judgment to reduce complexity.
  1. Domain depth in scientific or biomedical data platforms — genomics, bioinformatics, life sciences, or comparable data-intensive, workflow-driven scientific computing.
  1. Delivery inside a regulatory boundary such as FedRAMP, HIPAA, ISO 13485, or GxP.
  1. Reliability and modern delivery engineering: SLOs, error budgets, infrastructure-as-code, CI/CD with policy-as-code and progressive rollout.
  1. Production AI/LLM capability shipped under a compliance regime, or AI-assisted engineering you landed, governed and measured — beyond pilots.
  1. A track record of setting technical vision for a platform and carrying an organization there.
  1. Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field, or equivalent practical experience.

Nice to have

  • CWL/WDL/Nextflow, GA4GH standards (DRS/WES), FHIR or OMOP.
  • Federated or cross-institutional data access at scale — bringing analysis to data held by someone else.
  • Federal program delivery and artifact literacy — authorization packages, significant-change requests, and corrective-action plans.
  • Architecture depth in inference topology: hosting trade-offs, retrieval that inherits per-tenant authorization, evaluation harnesses, and guardrails.
  • Shipping reusable product capability out of grant- or program-funded work.

Competences

Vision

The ability to step back from the daily routine, explore ideas for the future, and see the platform in a broader context and in the longer term.

  • articulates where the platform must be in three years, and why
  • combines scientific, regulatory, and technology trends into one coherent direction
  • spots opportunities for the platform early and acts on them

Technical Depth

Personal command of the technology the platform is built on, enough to shape and challenge its biggest decisions.

  • reads code, designs, and test results first-hand rather than relying on summaries
  • changes a team’s technical direction with evidence rather than authority
  • is treated as a peer by senior engineers in design review

Managing

The ability to lead and develop others so they perform at their best — setting direction, providing the means, and holding the bar.

  • builds a management layer capable of running delivery without them, then holds it accountable
  • makes hiring and performance decisions promptly and explains them plainly
  • builds confidence and momentum and creates a thriving team environment

Focus on Quality

Setting high standards and treating quality, security, and compliance as design constraints rather than gates to be cleared.

  • designs for auditability, traceability, and reproducibility from the outset
  • converts recurring incidents into architectural and process change
  • declines shortcuts that would trade a compliance position for a delivery date

Decision Quality Under Ambiguity

The ability to make timely, defensible decisions on incomplete information, and to revisit them when the evidence changes.

  • commits to a sequence when the data is partial, and states what would change their mind
  • separates reversible from irreversible decisions and spends attention accordingly
  • records the reasoning as well as the outcome

Benefits

Our core values

People first. We create collaborative and supportive environments by operating with respect and flexibility to promote mental, emotional and physical health. We practice empathy by treating others the way they want to be treated and assuming positive intent. We are proud of our inclusive diverse team and humble ourselves to learn about and build our connection with each other.

Patient focused. We act with swift determination without sacrificing our expectations of quality. We are driven by providing exceptional solutions for our customers to positively impact patient lives. Considering what is at stake, we challenge ourselves to develop the best solution, not just the easy one.

Integrity. We hold ourselves accountable and strive for transparent communication to build trust amongst ourselves and our customers. We take ownership of our results as we know what we do matters and collectively we will change the healthcare industry. We are thoughtful and intentional with every customer interaction understanding the overall impact on human health.

Curious. We ask questions and actively listen in order to learn and continuously improve. We embrace change and the opportunities it presents to make each other better. We strive to be on the cutting edge of science and technology innovation by encouraging creativity.

Impactful. We take our social responsibility with the seriousness it deserves and hold ourselves to a high standard. We improve our sustainability by encouraging discussion and taking action as it relates to our natural, social and economic resource footprint. We are devoted to our humanitarian mission and look for new ways to make the world a better place.

Responsibilities

The Manager of Application Development owns the engineering team’s execution and the technical health, security, PCI compliance, and operational reliability of AgentMate, while partnering with Product and Delivery on approved priorities.

This is a hands-on management role for an experienced senior .NET engineer who can manage and mentor developers while remaining close to the code. The manager will translate business priorities into reliable software, help guide technical decisions, improve engineering discipline, and partner with product, delivery, infrastructure, security, and business teams to deliver secure, scalable, user-focused solutions.

A primary focus of this role is to ensure that AgentMate is secure, compliant, reliable, maintainable, and operationally sound, with particular emphasis on PCI requirements, application security, vulnerability management, secure development practices, access controls, data protection, and remediation of security risks.

The manager works closely with Information Security, Infrastructure, QA, Product, Delivery, and business stakeholders to ensure development activities meet established security, compliance, architectural, quality, and operational standards. The role supports product and business priorities from an engineering perspective but is not the primary owner of product strategy or roadmap direction.

Team Management

  • Lead, coach, and develop the AgentMate application development team, setting clear expectations for delivery, quality, security, collaboration, and accountability.
  • Plan and prioritize team capacity in partnership with product and delivery leaders; manage competing priorities, dependencies, production needs, and technical debt.
  • Conduct regular one-on-ones, provide timely feedback, support career development, and build succession and knowledge-sharing practices.
  • Create an inclusive, pragmatic engineering culture that values ownership, transparency, continuous learning, and measurable improvement.
  • Participate in hiring, onboarding, performance management, and resource planning for the application development team.

Hands-On Application Development

  • Remain actively involved in solution design, coding, code review, troubleshooting, and delivery for business-critical AgentMate capabilities.
  • Design, build, test, and maintain modern applications and services using C#, .NET/.NET Core, ASP.NET Core, RESTful APIs, SQL, and Azure-aligned services.
  • Guide the development of responsive, accessible user experiences using React, TypeScript, JavaScript, HTML, and CSS.
  • Promote maintainable engineering patterns, appropriate reuse, automated testing, clear documentation, and clean deployment practices.
  • Diagnose complex application issues across front-end, API, service, database, integration, and hosting layers.

Application Security and Risk Management

  • Embed secure software development practices throughout requirements, design, coding, testing, deployment, and support.
  • Lead application threat modeling, secure design reviews, security-focused code reviews, and remediation of identified vulnerabilities.
  • Apply practical knowledge of OWASP application security risks, authentication and authorization, identity and access management, secrets management, encryption, dependency risk, input validation, and secure API design.
  • Partner with Information Security and infrastructure teams on vulnerability scanning, penetration testing, incident response, audit support, and security control adoption.
  • Ensure applications, libraries, and third-party components are inventoried, monitored, patched, and upgraded in a risk-based and timely manner.
  • Coach developers on defensive coding and make security expectations part of the team’s definition of done.

Delivery, Quality, and Operations

  • Own engineering execution from technical discovery through production release and ongoing support, with clear visibility into risks, decisions, and progress.
  • Improve software quality through unit, integration, regression, performance, and security testing, with automation wherever practical.
  • Establish effective code review, branching, build, deployment, release, and rollback practices within CI/CD pipelines.
  • Improve application observability through actionable logging, monitoring, metrics, tracing, and alerting.
  • Lead root-cause analysis for significant defects or incidents and ensure durable corrective actions are completed.
  • Balance new feature delivery with modernization, reliability, maintainability, and reduction of technical debt.

Technical Direction and Collaboration

  • Provide technical direction for the AgentMate application while operating within established enterprise architecture, security, infrastructure, and technology standards.
  • Work closely with product owners, delivery managers, architects, security partners, QA, operations, and business stakeholders to shape feasible solutions and delivery plans.
  • Communicate technical tradeoffs, risks, dependencies, and recommendations clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Maintain current application, integration, data-flow, deployment, and support documentation sufficient for operational continuity.
  • Evaluate new technologies and patterns based on business value, security, supportability, cost, and team readiness rather than novelty.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Systems, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 8+ years of professional application development experience, including substantial hands-on experience with Microsoft .NET technologies.
  • 2+ years of formal people leadership, engineering management, team lead, or comparable experience with responsibility for coaching and delivery.
  • Advanced proficiency with C#, .NET/.NET Core, ASP.NET Core, RESTful APIs, SQL, object-oriented design, asynchronous programming, and modern testing practices.
  • Strong hands-on experience building and supporting modern web applications with React and TypeScript/JavaScript.
  • Demonstrated application security experience, including secure coding, threat modeling, vulnerability remediation, authentication/authorization, OWASP risks, dependency management, and secure API practices.
  • Experience with cloud-hosted applications and services, preferably Microsoft Azure, including CI/CD, monitoring, secrets/configuration management, and production support.
  • Experience integrating applications with internal and third-party services using APIs, messaging, and scheduled or event-driven processing.
  • Proven ability to lead technical delivery, make sound tradeoffs, manage risk, and communicate effectively across technical and business teams.
  • Willingness and ability to contribute directly to code, design, reviews, and incident resolution as team needs require.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience modernizing legacy .NET applications or decomposing tightly coupled systems in an incremental, low-risk manner.
  • PCI Professional (PCIP), Security+, CISSP, CSSLP, or comparable security certification.
  • Working knowledge of PCI DSS requirements and the application-development responsibilities associated with PCI compliance.

  • Experience with identity platforms and standards such as Microsoft Entra ID, OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, SAML, and role-based access control.

  • Familiarity with performance engineering, caching, resiliency patterns, distributed systems, and production observability.

We're looking for a CPA who wants to build something — not from scratch, and not alone, but with the freedom to shape a practice the way it should be shaped.

Our firm provides integrated financial care to physician families across California and several other U.S. states. We currently serve hundreds of households, and we're adding to the ways we serve them.

Today, our clients' tax and bookkeeping needs are served through external partner firms we've worked with for years. That partnership has helped us get to where we are, and it will continue. At the same time, we see meaningful gaps we'd like to fill ourselves — starting with bill pay and straightforward tax preparation. We'd like you to lead that work.

WHAT YOU'D BE BUILDING

A premium, integrated practice that complements the financial planning our clients already receive from us. You'd start with a built-in client base, an established brand, and something most CPAs building a practice never get: a global team of seasoned client service associates who handle first contact and administrative support. That means your time goes to the craft and the client conversations, not to sales, marketing, recruiting, legal, nor IT.

The practice is designed to evolve with our clients' needs over time, and you'll have a meaningful voice in how it grows.

WHAT YOU'D DO

  1. Provide bill pay services for elders and high-net-worth client families
  2. Prepare straightforward personal tax returns, primarily for W-2 households
  3. Shape how the practice grows, including how we manage the natural seasonality of tax work
  4. Collaborate with other team leaders to design repeatable systems that fit within our existing framework. Fitting in with our processes is essential.

YOU'LL ALSO BRING YOUR EXPERTISE TO

  1. Helping clients keep their financial records organized and decision-ready
  2. Guiding clients through entity-related questions that come up in their financial lives
  3. Bringing a tax-informed perspective into our team's planning conversations
  4. Being a trusted, knowledgeable resource for clients on the financial details that matter to them

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

  1. Licensed CPA in good standing
  2. Meaningful experience in tax preparation, with some exposure to bookkeeping
  3. Drawn to the idea of designing a practice rather than inheriting one
  4. A clear, warm communicator who genuinely enjoys client relationships
  5. Comfortable working remotely and collaborating across time zones
  6. Interested in the physician niche, or excited to learn it deeply

HOW WE WORK

We've been a fully distributed company since 2013, and over the years we've built a global team of seasoned client service associates who handle first contact and administrative support for every advisor, including you. Our shared priority is to protect your time for online conversations with clients.

Compensation is negotiable and tailored to the right person. We're open to W-2 with bonus or 1099, depending on what fits your situation and goals.

jobs.description:
Iovance Biotherapeutics aims to be the global leader in innovating, developing and delivering tumor infiltrating lymphocyte (TIL) therapy for people with cancer. We are pioneering a transformational approach to treating cancer by harnessing the ability of the human immune system to recognize and attack diverse cancer cells in each patient. The Iovance TIL platform has demonstrated promising clinical data across multiple solid tumors. We are committed to continuous innovation in cell therapy, including gene-edited cell therapy, which may be a promising option for patients with cancer.

Overview

This is a senior role responsible for the hands-on design, build, validation, and deployment of Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems at Iovance Biotherapeutics. This role is focused on execution — turning approved use cases into working, validated, production AI systems that deliver measurable business value. This role directly supports Iovance’s strategy to improve overall operational productivity. The ideal candidate is a deeply technical, hands-on senior engineer with demonstrated production experience designing and shipping Large Language Model (LLM) applications, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems, and modern AI integrations. This position works closely with IT leads, business process owners across Manufacturing, Quality, Regulatory Affairs, Clinical, Commercial, G&A, IT Security, Privacy, and Quality Assurance to deliver AI capabilities that respect Iovance’s regulated environment. This role executes against a roadmap and prioritized backlog, while contributing technical input to refinement, scoping, and sequencing.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Design, build, and ship AI systems against the approved Iovance AI roadmap, including end-to-end ownership of architecture, retrieval pipelines, prompts, evaluation, integrations, and deployment for assigned use cases.
  • Implement production-grade Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems on Iovance’s AWS infrastructure (S3, Redshift, Bedrock), including chunking strategies, embedding selection, vector storage, retrieval and reranking, grounding, and citation handling appropriate to high-accuracy use cases.
  • Build, maintain, and run evaluation harnesses for AI systems, including held-out test sets, accuracy and grounding metrics, hallucination detection, adversarial inputs, and regression testing across model and prompt changes; treat evaluation as a first-class engineering deliverable, not an afterthought.
  • Design and implement integrations between AI systems and Iovance enterprise systems using Model Context Protocol (MCP), APIs, and event-driven patterns, applying least-privilege access principles and partnering with IT Security on integration approval.
  • Own and maintain LLM security controls for production AI systems, including input and output guardrails, prompt injection and jailbreak defenses, sensitive data redaction (PII, PHI, Iovance Confidential Information and Intellectual Property), content moderation, and abuse monitoring, working in partnership with IT Security.
  • Design, develop, deploy, and maintain AI agents (multi-step reasoning systems that combine LLMs with tools, retrieval, and planning) appropriate for use in a regulated life sciences environment, including bounded scope, defined human oversight, traceability of agent decisions, and safe handling of write-back actions to systems of record
  • Establish and uphold modern engineering practices for AI development including version control for code, prompts, and evaluation sets; CI/CD pipelines; environment separation (dev, test, production); and reproducible builds.
  • Conduct hands-on technical evaluation of AI vendors, tools, and Foundation Models when build-vs-buy decisions are under consideration; produce concise, fact-based recommendations to the IT function lead and AI Governance Committee, including proof-of-concept results where appropriate.
  • Implement and operate technical controls for production AI systems including audit logging, access management, prompt and model change control, model registry, ongoing performance monitoring, and incident detection, in alignment with Iovance policies.
  • Author technical documentation appropriate to the system risk tier, including architecture diagrams, data flow diagrams, evaluation reports, runbooks, and validation deliverables; contribute to the Iovance AI Validation Playbook.
  • Mentor junior engineers who collaborate on AI projects; stay current on rapid advances in AI tooling, models, and engineering best practices, and bring technical recommendations forward.

Qualifications

  • 10+ years of progressive software and/or AI/ML engineering experience, with the most recent 1+ years dedicated primarily to LLM-based application development. Demonstrated track record of shipping production AI systems that real users depend on.
  • Deep, hands-on production experience with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) including chunking strategies, embedding models, vector stores, retrieval and reranking, and grounding for high-accuracy use cases. Working production experience with Model Context Protocol (MCP) or equivalent agent/tool integration patterns.
  • Practical working experience across multiple frontier model families (e.g., Anthropic Claude, OpenAI GPT, Google Gemini, leading open-weight models), with the judgment to select among them based on task fit, accuracy, cost, latency, safety properties, and data-handling commitments. Awareness of model capability changes and how to evaluate new model releases.
  • Strong software engineering fundamentals: production Python (and ideally one other language); modern Agile delivery; version control (Git); CI/CD; containerization; cloud platforms (preferably AWS, with working familiarity with S3, Redshift, and Bedrock); MLOps tooling and practices.
  • Hands-on, builder disposition; this role spends the majority of its time writing code, designing systems, evaluating models, and producing technical artifacts — not in meetings.
  • Working production experience with AWS data and AI services is strongly preferred (S3, Redshift, Bedrock, IAM).
  • Working knowledge of enterprise search and retrieval services such as OpenSearch, Elasticsearch, or equivalent, including the design of hybrid retrieval patterns (vector plus lexical/BM25) that improve grounding and relevance in production RAG systems

Preferred/Desirable Knowledge, Skills, and Education

  • Relevant cloud and AI/ML certifications (AWS, Azure, etc.);
  • Working knowledge of US regulatory requirements applicable to AI in regulated life sciences, including 21 CFR Part 11, GxP, HIPAA, and emerging FDA expectations on AI/ML in pharmaceutical manufacturing and drug development
  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Engineering, or related quantitative discipline.

Physical Demands and Activities Required

  • Must be able to remain in a stationary position standing or sitting for prolonged periods of time.
  • Must be able to move about inside an office and exert up to 10 pounds of force occasionally or a negligible amount of force frequently or constantly to lift, carry, push, pull, or otherwise move objects.
  • Must have visual acuity to perform activities such as: preparing and analyzing data and figures, viewing a computer screen, and extensive reading.
  • This position requires repetitive motion, substantial movements (motions) of the wrist, hands, and/or fingers.
  • Must be able to communicate with others to exchange information.

Mental: Clear and conceptual thinking ability; excellent judgment, troubleshooting, problem-solving, analysis, and discretion; ability to handle work-related stress; ability to handle multiple priorities simultaneously; and ability to meet deadlines.

Work Environment

This job operates in a professional workplace or remote office environment and requires standard office equipment and keyboards. Employees who work remotely are expected to maintain their workspace and environment safely and free from safety hazards.

Why Talkspace?

Talkspace is the world’s leading online therapy company, serving over 2 million users looking to begin their wellness journey through tele-health. How do we define Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Belonging at Talkspace?

Diversity

Diversity encompasses the unique attributes of our employees as individuals. We value and embrace the richness arising from their varied backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences, which include, but are not limited to, age, ability, ethnicity, gender, race, and cultural background.

Equity

Equity refers to a fair and impartial workplace, aiming to ensure equal growth and advancement opportunities for all employees. This involves amplifying underrepresented voices, addressing unconscious biases, and providing inclusive, culturally competent mental health care.

Inclusion

Inclusion signifies the practice of granting equal access to opportunities and resources for all employees, particularly those who might otherwise be excluded or marginalized. It ensures that everyone feels a sense of belonging, value, support, and respect as an individual.

Belonging

Belonging reflects the affinity and positive relationships that develop among employees from diverse backgrounds when businesses actively promote diversity, equity, and inclusion in the workplace.
